# step177-truth-rejected-as-single-predicate

**Scope(s):** THEORY-LEVEL · **Row count:** 3 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** DORMANT · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** Approved(ArchitectureX,Organization,t) instead of ArchitectureX=UniversallyBestArchitecture, Formal/Deterministic/Empirical/Statistical/Interpretive/Authoritative epistemic modes, Supported(x)/Established(x)/Valid(x,t,S)/Approved(x,t)/Authorized(x,t) instead of Truth(x) · **Aliases:** KnowledgeOS should not model truth as one predicate
**Candidate group membership (NOT an identity claim):**
Ungrouped — no mechanical signal connected this label to any other in P2a.


## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)
- **OBJECT-INDEX**, batch `B0033`, scope `THEORY-LEVEL`: Step 177's central verdict: KnowledgeOS should not model 'truth' as a single undifferentiated state/predicate Truth(x); instead it should use multiple owned predicates -- Supported(x), Established(x), Valid(x,t,S), Approved(x,t), Authorized(x,t) -- each belonging to a different domain owner (EpistemicStatus to the epistemic model, ApprovalStatus to governance, AuthorizationStatus to authorization, ExecutionStatus to operations; the same word 'status' hides completely different domain meanings across these). Illustrates with an authoritative-but-not-universally-true fact: an Architecture Board decision is captured as Approved(ArchitectureX,Organization,t), never as ArchitectureX=UniversallyBestArchitecture. Provisionally proposes a mode-of-justification taxonomy (Formal, Deterministic, Empirical, Statistical, Interpretive, Authoritative), explicitly not yet frozen -- a hypothesis for later experiments -- distinguishing e.g. formal arithmetic truth (1+1=2) from an empirical engineering proposition (zero-downtime migration claim).
